messages:
customer-bob: Hey team — hitting a weird pattern on our Dedicated pool. Around 09:12 UTC our calls started getting intermittent 429s for ~30s windows even though our dashboard shows reserved capacity available. Latency spikes at same time (p50 ~120ms -> 850ms). No changes on our side. Posting curl output and headers. Anyone seen this?

customer-bob: ```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-App: mobile-payments
X-Req-ID: r-9bd3

{
  "model":"rwd-dedicated-1",
  "input":"hello"
}
---
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2024 09:12:18 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 9
```

customer-bob: We do short bursts from many clients (mobile devices) — traffic pattern is spiky. Curious if this is reserved-pool misalignment or global rate shaping kicking in.

support-jordan: Thanks for the report — sorry about the disruption. Can you paste the account id and the dedicated pool id (or confirm which subscription)? Also roughly how many concurrent connections / qps during the bursts?

customer-bob: Account: acct_9f8e
Pool id: pool-us-west-3
We saw ~180 qps for ~15s bursts coming from ~2k mobile clients (connection-level concurrency lower, around 100 concurrent keep-alive sockets).

support-jordan: Got it. Two probable causes: 1) per-account token-level rate caps are being hit (burst credits exhausted), 2) global control-plane smoothing to preserve latency SLOs is throttling sudden spikes (especially if sustained across model variants). I'm going to pull the server-side logs.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20240705-0926 (auto-detected spike vs reserved pool). Linked: https://incidents.redwood/in/INC-20240705-0926

eng-kate: Copying in runtime team. Early question: are requests using streaming or non-streaming endpoints? Streaming changes the token accounting and kv-cache reuse.

customer-bob: Non-streaming gen calls. Small payloads.

eng-kate: OK. Please do a repro with a steady 200 qps for 60s for one IP (or controlled worker) and attach request ids. We want to see whether the 429s align with a token bucket refill boundary or a pool-level enqueue failure. While you run it, enable debug header `X-Debug-Trace: 1` so our logs have the routed backend ids.

ops-ash: I'm checking the pool capacity and allocator metrics for pool-us-west-3 — nothing obvious on reserved GPU allocation side, but I see short-lived queue depth spikes at 09:12:10-09:12:45 that correlate with SLO-preserving rate-limiter events. Those are the global "burst-fence" policies kicking in when sustained burstiness threatens tail latency.

linus: Quick note on behavior: reserved pools have two levers — guaranteed throughput (the reserved tokens) and burst credits. If many small clients each consume request credit concurrently, the burst pool can be exhausted quickly and then the account falls back to the shared rate-cap which is much lower. That looks consistent with Remaining=0 in your header.

support-jordan: For immediate mitigation: 1) implement client-side smoothing (random jitter + token bucket local to the mobile app) to reduce fan-out. 2) add exponential backoff with Retry-After respect. 3) if acceptable, route high-throughput features through a server-side aggregator to reduce connection cardinality.

customer-bob: Do you have a recommended config for token bucket / smoothing? Mobile devices are unreliable for long-lasting queues.

linus: Suggested quick rules: allow bursts up to 3x steady qps with a refill window of ~60s; on client, use leaky-bucket with capacity=3*rate, refill=rate/60s, jitter +/-20%. On server-side, set per-route concurrency limit. If you can't change clients quickly, we can offer a short-term uplift on your reserved burst credits while you migrate.

eng-kate: We're going to check whether the pool's smoothing thresholds need tuning for this account. Two options: 1) allow per-pool higher short-window burst by adjusting the pool's short-term token bucket, 2) create a dedicated "burst lane" for pool-us-west-3 for the next 24h while customers migrate. Ops, can we do a temporary policy change for acct_9f8e?

ops-ash: I can open a temporary policy: bump short-window burst by 2x for acct_9f8e within pool-us-west-3 for 6 hours; requires approval from platform SRE. If you want permanent, we'll need fix + perf tests.

support-jordan: Customer — would you like the 6-hour uplift now while you perform client smoothing?

customer-bob: Yes please, that would help with production traffic while we rollout a server aggregator.

support-jordan: Done. Ops: please action the uplift and confirm.

ops-ash: Policy change applied: acct_9f8e short-burst-multiplier=2 (effective 2024-07-05T09:34:12Z). Monitoring for the next hour.

sre-bot: AUTO: Alert cleared for INC-20240705-0926 (spike mitigated).

customer-bob: Thanks, I see 429s drop after the change and latency stabilizes. We'll follow your smoothing guidance.

eng-kate: Followups: can you share the reproduction run logs with `X-Debug-Trace` IDs? We'll analyze whether throttle points were at front-proxy, pool enqueue, or per-account limiter.

customer-bob: Will do — spinning up repro now and will paste the request ids in this thread.

support-jordan: Closing the escalation for now; keeping thread open until repro + logs collected. If you hit regressions after client rollout, ping this thread and we'll re-open and consider capacity resize or a permanent pool policy change. :thumbsup:
